title: A Survey on Fairness in Large Language Models
findings: The survey consolidates findings that Large Language Models (LLMs) consistently exhibit biases related to religion. For instance, GPT-3 was found to show higher levels of violent prejudice against Muslims compared to other religious groups. Models tend to rely on social biases, including religious stereotypes, to make predictions when contextual information is insufficient. The level and nature of bias can vary; for example, GPT models may show higher bias on less sensitive topics (e.g., leadership) than on more sensitive topics like terrorism, and can be tricked into agreeing with stereotypes in misleading scenarios.

measurement_description: The survey reviews benchmarks that measure social biases, including stereotypes and prejudice against various religious groups. Specific measurements include quantifying stereotypical associations in sentence completions, analyzing co-occurrence frequencies of religious terms with positive/negative/violent content, evaluating toxicity in generated text when prompted with religious identifiers, and assessing performance disparities in question-answering tasks with ambiguous religious contexts.
